According to Tuesday’s filing in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, the parties agreed to two days of negotiations beginning October 14. Prior to the start of negotiations, the two sides will file statements supporting their respective positions surrounding the merger, including an evaluation of the “likelihood of prevailing” and major issues in dispute.
The court order also gives representatives for all parties the full authority to negotiate and settle the case. Bonta is seeking concessions from Paramount
that include selling parts of the merged companies, while Paramount
has so far offered only "behavioral concessions" such as a commitment to release at least 30 films.
